questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to Jordan mainly because I wanted to learn the levantic Arabic dialect (Jordanian/Palestinian). Jordan, and the capital Amman is also a very interesting destination because of it diverse culture and population. The University of Jordans' Language Center to learn Arabic does also have a good reputation and I had a good impression of it from other students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: In generall I did not have any problems, I got a lot of information from Erasmus and the Erasmus office at the university were very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got assistance from the Erasmus office. They showed my around at the university and helped me with all the papers I had to fill in for my stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. First I found a room through a Facebook group for apartments in Amman. Later I moved, and then I found a place through some friends. It was very easy to find a place to stay, none of has had any problem to find a room.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It gives you the opportunity to discover more areas of the city on a daily basis. It may also give you a more local experience. It's important to remember thet public transpotration and the traffic is very different from European cityes. You may use a lot of time on transportation to the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I only went to an office and filled in my information, it was very easy because almost everything was registrered before I came through Erasmus.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The people at the Erasmus office helped.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: We used the first weeks to go to different classes to see witch level was best for us, therefore I could stay at the level I was comfortable in. I did not have to registrer anything before.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Arrive around one week before your classes start so you have time to settle and registrer. It is also good to think about how much time you want to use for school work. For example if you choose a hard level, you will learn a lot of arabic but you need a lot of time to study. It's also possible to choose an easier level and use more time to get to know the country. It all depends on what you want to use your time on and if you learn arabic best form classes or from making local friends.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: There are nine levels. One is beginner and nine is almost native speaker. The levels may be fluent because people choose the courses themselves, in my class some people spoke fluent while some spoke basics.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Both places has a close class where you get to know everyone, and the people are very friendly. A part from the beginner levels the teachers only speak arabic in class, which was different from UCPH, but I learn a lot from it.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I was in level 6 at the Language Center.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depends on their level. If they have studied arabic for 1,5 years like me, I would recoment level 4 or 5.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Taxi is around 20-30 DKK, but I got suprised that you have to take taxi all the time and then it's expensive in the end.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The gym is very expensive (500-1000DKK) every month, alcohol is also more expensive than in Denmark. Sunscreen is also very expensive. In bigger supermarkets the food may be a bit expensive. If you go to the smaller supermarkets and local restaurants the food is very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dabke dance, football and calligraphy. I think there are more that I don't know about.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them at the university. I also recommend to go the Jordan Trail that has a lot of hikes and there are also a lot of yoga classes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recomment the trips with the university that goes almost every weekend to different parts of the country, it's cheaper than travelling by yourself. I recoment The Dead Sea, Wadi Rum, Petra, Wadi Mujib, Um Qais and Aqaba.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is a very different culture and you should be prepared for that. It was not hard but you will get some surprises and questions you will never get in Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Have a language partners. In generall people, are very open, especially at the university. It's easy to talk to people on the bus, on the street etc. In general people are very intrested in talking to foregniers. Note that it's not normal for all Jordanians to socialize between genders.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Gender equality is not the same as in Denmark. Talking to men, you sometimes have to be very clear of your own boundaries.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The hospitality. People are very welcoming and always care about you a lot.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1: Don't compare everything to Denmark, or think that everything is better in Denmark. 
2. The people at the language center are usally alone in a new country too. They are very nice and easy to be friends with.
3. If you have questions about the culture, don't be afraid to ask! People are very to happy to explain and tell you about their culture.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: In Jordanian culture time works very different than in Denmark. People are more spontaneous and might not follow a schedule. Try to see the value of that, it's very relaxing, even dough it might feel wierd in the beginning.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends from so many countries and cultures and learning a lot of arabic in a small amount of time.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Learning to understand the local dialect in the beginning. It felt a bit frustraiting in the beginning to not understand anything, after studying arabic before, but after some time I learnt a lot.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
